title: Index on Computed Column
description: Learn how to simulate function-based indexes using indexes on computed columns.

data.text: SQL Server Index on Computed Column
In SQL Server, you can use an index on a computed column to achieve the similar effect of a function-based index. This is useful when queries use expressions in their WHERE clause.

items: First, create a computed column based on the expression in the WHERE clause.
Second, create a nonclustered index for the computed column.

data.content: Creates a computed column for the local part of an email and indexes it.

data.text: Requirements for Indexes on Computed Columns

items: Functions in the expression must have the same owner as the table.
The expression must be deterministic (same result for same inputs).
The expression must be precise (no FLOAT or REAL data types).
The result cannot evaluate to TEXT, NTEXT, or IMAGE.
ANSI_NULLS, ANSI_PADDING, ANSI_WARNINGS, ARITHABORT, QUOTED_IDENTIFIER, and CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL must be ON.

data.title: Computed Column Index Key Points
points: Indexes on computed columns simulate function-based indexes in SQL Server.
The computed column expression must be deterministic and precise.
They improve query performance for WHERE clauses with expressions.
Several SET options must be ON when defining the computed column.
